parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Deduce the empirical formula of vitamin C.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
The mass of vitamin C present in $150.0\text{ g}$ of lemon is found in an experiment.

**stage 1** All the vitamin C in $150.0\text{ g}$ of lemon is extracted and dissolved in water to make $100.0\text{ cm}^3$ of solution **L**.

**stage 2** A $25.0\text{ cm}^3$ sample of solution **L** is titrated with $5.00 \times 10^{-3}\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ $\text{I}_2\text{(aq)}$.

{{figure:pdf_visual_02.png}}

Fig. 5.2

Exactly $36.65\text{ cm}^3$ of $\text{I}_2\text{(aq)}$ reacts with the $25.0\text{ cm}^3$ sample of solution **L**.

[$M_{\text{r}}$: vitamin C, 176]

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Calculate the amount, in mol, of $\text{I}_2\text{(aq)}$ added in the titration.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
Use your answer to **(b)(i)** to calculate the percentage by mass of vitamin C present in $150.0\text{ g}$ of lemon.

(If you were unable to calculate a value for the amount of $\text{I}_2\text{(aq)}$ in **(b)(i)**, use the value $7.65 \times 10^{-4}\text{ mol}$. This is **not** the correct value.)
